chapter: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
title: Hired for the band at the Crystal Caverns
summary: The most prestigious U Street nightclub, home of Cavernism, needs a pianist, and he joins an eight-piece show band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Then I was offered this job at a place on Eleventh and U called... Then it was called the Crystal Caverns, which was where Tommy Miles' band had worked some years before. And Jimmy Mundy had written this very popular, or I would say famous tune of his called "Cavernism" that Earl Hines' band later made popular. Anyway, it was all written right there in this place called The Crystal Caverns, which I guess was probably the most prestigious nightclub on U Street. So someone said that they needed a pianist down there to play with the band. I don't know exactly how it happened. I think someone told them about me while I was working at this club, the Jungle Inn.

So the fact that I'm going to work down at the Caverns was just like I guess someone saying you've got a job in the Waldorf-Astoria somewhere. It was a big, big deal, you know? And I knew they had chorus lines down there, they had an eight-piece band, and never really realizing what I was going into... I just had enough ego to feel like I could do it.

So I went down there, and it happened that I knew a few of the guys in that band, because they also used to come up and jam with me, up at this place -- at the Atlantic Beer Garden. So I went in, they all welcomed me and everything. And the leader... I don't remember who he was or what his name was, but he was one of the guys. So they said, "Rehearsals will start in about a half-hour, and as soon as all the principals get here..." There were these girls -- I've forgotten how many of them there were. As a matter of fact, I don't know if they had dancers and comedians, or a comedian or something... But anyway, it was a full show, and the show was about an hour and a half long.
